whatItIs: A two-skill Claude/Codex plugin by Niksa Barlovic, v1.1.0, MIT, inside the wshobson/agents marketplace (39.5k stars). grounded-vault (SKILL.md 105 lines + references/details.md 207 lines, added 2026-09-01 from issue #673) teaches a three-layer Markdown store — raw/ immutable sources, wiki/ compiled pages, archive/ superseded pages — where each page carries a four-field header (Raw:, Fingerprint: git:<sha>, Monitored: <code paths>, Status: Current|Outdated|Disputed), every figure or quotation in prose links to the source it came from, and staleness is detected by `git diff --stat <fingerprint>..HEAD -- <monitored paths>` instead of re-reading code. details.md ships a ~110-line stdlib-only check_vault.py that does both checks, plus a pre-commit hook and CI step. hads (190 lines, added 2026-03-21) is an unrelated tagging convention: four bold block tags (**[SPEC]** / **[NOTE]** / **[BUG]** / **[?]**) plus a mandatory "AI READING INSTRUCTION" manifest telling the model which blocks to read and skip. It is document-structure dogma for machine readers, asserted end to end; its own validator is marked "planned — not yet included in this release" (hads/SKILL.md:135). Neither skill is about prose quality for a human reader; grounded-vault is about provenance and drift on a knowledge store, which is why it is an adjacent — not competing — approach to terse.
measures: Almost nothing about text quality. The only numbers it produces are two counts from check_vault.py: grounding misses (figures/quotes in prose absent from the linked source) and drifted pages (monitored code changed since the fingerprint); details.md:113 prints "N problem(s)". There is no evaluation of whether the pattern makes documents better, faster to read, or more correct — no reader test, no A/B, no token accounting in the repo. The only supporting evidence anywhere is the proposer's unquantified anecdote in issue #673 ("it cut our re-read tokens a lot", "git diff checks drift in 0.01s instead of re-reading the codebase"). The "zero-token" and "runs in milliseconds" claims (SKILL.md:75, plugin.json:4) are mechanically true by construction, not measured. I measured one thing myself: the drift check fires correctly on a monitored-file edit, and the grounding check both catches a genuinely absent figure and falsely rejects a genuinely present one.

practices.practice: Stamp each document with the commit it was written against and the list of code paths it describes ('Fingerprint: git:5b237fa' / 'Monitored: src/auth/jwt.ts, package.json'), then decide whether to re-audit by running `git diff --stat <fingerprint>..HEAD -- <monitored paths>`: empty output means the document still describes the code it was compiled against, any output means recompile and re-stamp. Treat a fingerprint git can no longer resolve (history rewrite) as drift.
practices.locus: plugins/documentation-standards/skills/grounded-vault/SKILL.md:41-53 and :67-75; rule for unresolvable fingerprints at references/details.md:136-138
practices.evidenceForIt: Argued mechanically, not measured; the author's token-saving claim in issue #673 is unquantified. I verified the mechanism end to end: editing a monitored file made the shipped script report 'drifted since git:09efcd4' with the diffstat, and it stayed silent when only unmonitored files changed.
practices.costAndCollision: Near-zero to run. Direct fit for terse: an audit that spends one fresh model per question is expensive, and this gives a free trigger for when the answer key derived from code has gone stale. Collides with 'no noise' if the header is printed in the reader-facing page — for terse, keep the fingerprint in a sidecar or audit record, not in the prose a human reads.

practices.practice: Treat every number, date and direct quotation as a claim that must appear verbatim in its named source, and check it by exact-token search rather than by rereading: the figure must match as a whole token (15 must not satisfy 150 or 2015), a quotation must match character for character, and a reformatted figure (1,000 vs 1000) is a miss on purpose — copy the source's form. Exclude the header block, headings, fenced code and the labels/paths of links from the scan so a path like raw/adr/0007-jwt.md never reads as a claim of 0007.
practices.locus: plugins/documentation-standards/skills/grounded-vault/SKILL.md:55-63; rule list at references/details.md:121-139; implementation at references/details.md:23-27 and :63-72
practices.evidenceForIt: Argued, with a runnable implementation, and partly refuted by running it: the exclusion rules work (link paths did not register as claims), the true-miss detection works, but the whole-token guard has a verified false-positive class (see weaknesses). The idea survives; that implementation does not.
practices.costAndCollision: Cheap and it mechanises exactly the 'lie' class that terse's audit already classifies by hand. Cost: it only works against a text corpus, so for terse the source of truth has to be the code/config, which needs a different extractor than a grep for literals in Markdown. Collision risk with the rejected 'prose linters as a gate': this is a factual-claim checker, not a style checker, so it is a different kind of rule — but it must ship as a report, not a gate (next item).

practices.practice: Run the literal-fidelity check as a report, never as an auto-fix or a commit gate: call its output 'fidelity suspects, not verdicts', require a human or model to compare each suspect against the source context, and report only real mismatches. Keep a separate, smaller class of hard errors (missing source field, unresolvable link, link escaping the source directory) that demand a decision.
practices.locus: PALAN-K/llm-wiki-loop skills/wiki-manager/references/wiki-protocol.md:126-136 ('Mechanical reports (script — never auto-fix)') — contrast with plugins/documentation-standards/skills/grounded-vault/SKILL.md:91-98, which repackages the same check as `--strict` exiting 1 from a pre-commit hook and CI
practices.evidenceForIt: Asserted by the upstream author; the divergence between the two documents is itself documented fact, and my run supplies the reason the upstream framing is right — the gate version blocks a commit on a correct page.
practices.costAndCollision: Free, and it is the framing that survives the owner's standing rejection of CI gates. Adopting the wshobson version instead would import a rejected pattern.

practices.practice: When a figure cannot be located in a source, do not write it in exact form at all; and for any derived value (a sum, a delta, a percentage) state its components so each component stays traceable to a source.
practices.evidenceForIt: Asserted, no measurement. It is the writing-side rule that the mechanical check is the enforcement of — the only item here that changes what an author types rather than what a script reports.
practices.costAndCollision: Free. Compatible with terse's 'prove, don't assert' spine; no collision.

practices.practice: Correct knowledge by superseding, not deleting: a page contradicted by a newer source gets 'Status: Disputed', a page whose subject moved on gets 'Status: Outdated' with a one-line reason naming the cause and the date, and is moved to archive/ rather than removed. Skip non-Current pages in the fidelity check — they are records, not claims. Every add, move or archive updates the index and appends one line to an append-only log in the same commit.
practices.locus: plugins/documentation-standards/skills/grounded-vault/SKILL.md:19, :31, :53, :82-89; skip rule at references/details.md:139; log format at references/details.md:166-171
practices.evidenceForIt: Asserted. No measurement; the templates are plausible and the skip rule is a sound consequence of the status field.
practices.costAndCollision: Cheap. Mild collision with 'no noise': an index plus a log plus status headers is real ceremony for a small repo, and terse's own measured wins came from rewriting prose, not from bookkeeping. Worth taking only for documents that get re-audited repeatedly.

practices.practice: Never ground a compiled page on another compiled page — compiled pages cite immutable sources only, and a link that escapes the source directory or points at a missing file counts as a grounding miss.
practices.evidenceForIt: Asserted, with enforcement code. I confirmed the resolution guard exists (raw_source() rejects anything not inside the resolved raw/ root) but did not test the escape case.
practices.costAndCollision: Free as a rule. For terse the analogue is: an answer key derives from code, never from another document — which the audit design already assumes; this is corroboration rather than a new idea.

practices.practice: For sources that are not plain text, make them checkable rather than exempt: store a binary in the source layer together with a sibling text extraction produced once by a deterministic tool and cite the text file; for an external URL, save a dated snapshot into the source layer and cite the snapshot, keeping the URL on the snapshot's first line for attribution, because a URL is not immutable.
practices.costAndCollision: Low cost, narrow benefit. Only pays off where a doc cites PDFs or web pages; irrelevant to a code-grounded audit.

weaknesses:
Three substantive problems, one of them proven by running the code.

1. The shipped check script has a verified false-positive class that would block correct commits. The whole-token guard is `(?<![\w.,])15(?![\w.,])` (details.md:64), so a figure that appears in the source immediately before a period or comma is unfindable. Proven: with the source line "The retry budget is 15 attempts." and the page sentence "...for the budget of 15." the script printed `wiki/auth3.md: '15.' not found in ../raw/adr/0007-jwt.md` and exited 1, even though 15 is present verbatim. Two defects combine: the claim regex `\d[\d.,]*` (details.md:25) greedily swallows the sentence-final period into the claim, and the lookahead then refuses to match a source figure that is itself sentence-final. Isolated regex probe: 'budget is 15.' → False, 'budget is 15, and' → False, 'budget is 15 attempts' → True. details.md:126-128 documents the 1,000-vs-1000 rejection as deliberate but says nothing about sentence-final figures — this is a bug, not a design choice, and it is wired into a pre-commit hook at details.md:173-181. Same lookahead also means some sentence-final claims in the page are silently never scanned, so `--strict` has false negatives too.

2. Undocumented runtime floor. check_vault.py uses `Path | None` in an evaluated annotation (details.md:57), which raises `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for |: 'type' and 'NoneType'` on Python 3.9 (reproduced on this machine's 3.9.16); it needs 3.10+. The skill says only "standard library and git" (details.md:10-11).

3. The check does not cover the thing terse cares about. Grounding is verified only against text files under raw/ (details.md:51, :57-60); claims about code are never checked for truth. The drift check covers code but only reports that monitored files changed — it cannot say whether the document is now wrong. So the pair detects "a figure is not in a note" and "code moved", never "the document misleads a reader". That is the gap terse's reader-scored audit fills, and it is why this is adjacent rather than competing.

Also recorded, not recommended: hads/SKILL.md. It is a pure assertion — its validator is "planned — not yet included in this release" (hads/SKILL.md:135), its central claim that the AI manifest "lets even small (7B) models know what to read and what to skip" (hads/SKILL.md:165) carries no evidence, and its content rule "Maximum 2 sentences of prose — if more needed, move to [NOTE]" (hads/SKILL.md:113) is a hard length cap of the class already rejected on evidence. Its tag-block structure is a document-structure standard of exactly the kind that lost to unguided controls in the 2026-09-10 bake-off. Do not adopt as a pass; keep as a data point that a 39.5k-star marketplace ships structure-first doc dogma with a planned-but-absent validator.

Provenance is thin by design: the plugin is a repackaging of one 13-star project (PALAN-K/llm-wiki-loop, MIT, last pushed 2026-08-21), proposed by its own author in issue #673 and merged 11 days later; the wshobson copy hardens the upstream's report-only lint into a blocking gate without saying so.

Out of scope but noted for a later round: the same repo ships plugins/plugin-eval/ and docs/plugin-eval.md, described in README.md:118-132 as a three-layer skill-quality evaluation framework with an LLM judge. I did not open either file and make no claim about their contents.
